name: The Johannine Epistles: Truth, Light, and Love
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify from 1 John that God is love and that he showed his love by sending his Son
Recite 1 John 4:19 and tell how God's love for us comes before our love for him and for others
Identify from 1 John that God is light with no darkness in him
Recite 1 John 1:9 and explain that John teaches we should confess our sins to God, who promises to forgive
Describe practical ways to love others in deed and truth as John commands, using Jesus laying down his life as the pattern
Explain what it means that Jesus is our Advocate with the Father when believers sin
Summarize John's contrast between walking in the light and walking in the darkness
Explain from 1 John 3 what it means to be called children of God and how the tradition confesses this as adoption
Explain how John presents keeping God's commandments and loving fellow believers as evidence of knowing God
Compare love of the world with love of the Father using the three desires John names
Explain how John says faith in Jesus as the Son of God overcomes the world
Describe John's teaching on confident prayer according to God's will and practice writing a prayer shaped by it
Identify the traditional author, audience, and occasion of 1, 2, and 3 John, including the role of the elder
Identify the spirit of antichrist as John describes it, especially the denial that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh
Explain the meaning of propitiation in 1 John and how it shows the source of God's love
Analyze the recurring tests of true belief in 1 John, namely right belief about Christ, obedience, and love
Explain John's teaching on fellowship with the Father, the Son, and one another and what breaks it
Compare the prologue of 1 John with the prologue of the Gospel of John, noting shared themes of the Word, life, and eyewitness testimony
Contrast the purpose statement of 1 John with that of the Gospel of John
Interpret the statement that perfect love casts out fear within its context of confidence on the day of judgment
Interpret John's statements about not practicing sin and about the sin leading to death in light of his teaching that believers still sin
Compare the conduct of Gaius, Diotrephes, and Demetrius in 3 John and what each shows about faithful church life
Construct a biblical definition of agape love from the Johannine epistles
Analyze the textual evidence for the longer reading of 1 John 5:7-8 and explain why the doctrine of the Trinity does not depend on it
Evaluate the grounds of assurance of salvation that John gives and compare them with the Reformed confession of assurance
Defend the true humanity and incarnation of Christ from the Johannine epistles against docetic and proto-Gnostic teaching
Synthesize the teaching of 2 and 3 John on when to extend and when to withhold hospitality for the sake of truth

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (God is love, Advocate, confession of sin, light and darkness, children of God, world vs Father, antichrist, tests of life, perfect love, link to John's Gospel, sin leading to death, agape, assurance, incarnation, hospitality). Turned the K-3 recall items into specific, verse-anchored objectives and replaced 'Observe that we must love one another' with practical love in deed and truth. Split the Gospel connection into prologue comparison and purpose statements. Added missing content: God is light, we love because he first loved, propitiation, adoption confession, overcoming the world, prayer by God's will, historical setting, fellowship, 3 John characters, and the 1 John 5:7-8 textual issue. Added confessional anchors where they state the doctrine and corrected scripture ranges.
